title: Fabricating Degradable Thermoresponsive Hydrogels on Multiple Length Scales via Reactive Extrusion, Microfluidics, Self-assembly, and Electrospinning
protocol: Weigh out 37 mg of AIBMe initiator.
Weigh out 3.1 g of diethylene glycol methacrylate (M(EO)2MA).
Weigh out 0.9 g of oligoethyleneglycol methacrylate (OEGMA475).
Measure 523 µL of acrylic acid (AA).
Measure 7.5 µL of thiolglycolic acid (TGA).
Dissolve all reagents in dioxane at a ratio of 5 mL/g total monomer.
Purge the reaction mixture with nitrogen for 30 min.
Place the reaction flask in a pre-heated oil bath maintained at 75 °C.
Maintain the reaction under nitrogen and stir at 400 rpm magnetic stirring for 4 h.
Remove the solvent using a rotary evaporator set to 50 °C and 200 rpm.
Dissolve the resulting polymer product in 150 mL of deionized water.
Add adipic acid dihydrizide (ADH) at a five-fold molar excess to the number of AA residues incorporated into the polymer.
Adjust the pH of the solution to pH 4.75 using 0.1 M HCl.
Add N-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)-N'-ethylcarbodiimide (EDC) at a 5-fold molar excess to the number of AA residues present.
Maintain the reaction pH 4.75 with dropwise addition of 0.1 M HCl over 4 h.
Leave the reaction to stir overnight.
Pour the product solution into three ~30 cm long dialysis tubes (3500 Da molecular weight cut-off, 1 inch thickness).
Use a pinch clamp to close the bottom and top of each tube prior to filling by folding a small (~2 cm) segment of the tube.
Place the tubes inside a 100-fold excess volume of deionized water for at least 6 h.
Fully replace the water over six cycles of dialysis to achieve desired purity.
Lyophilize the dialyzed sample to obtain a final dried polymer product.
Place 200 mL of a 20% w/v NaOH solution into a 500 mL 3 neck round-bottom flask.
Cool the solution in an ice bath and maintain a temperature of 0 °C with ice during the reaction.
Add 50 mL of aminoacetyl aldehyde dimethyl acetal to the cooled NaOH solution.
Add 0.1 g of TEMPO to the mixture and stir at 400 rpm until fully dissolved.
Add 48 mL of methacryloyl chloride dropwise using a burette over 2 h.
Cover the reaction vessel with aluminum foil and leave to stir overnight.
Extract the product by adding it to 75 mL of petroleum ether in a separation funnel, shaking, degassing, and discarding the top layer.
Repeat extraction three times with the bottom layer as raw material for each cycle.
Remove the final bottom layer product and transfer to a 100 mL beaker.
Add ~5 g magnesium sulfate (Mg2SO4) to the beaker until a "snow globe" effect is observed.
Filter through a 100 mL Buchner funnel to remove Mg2SO4.
Rinse the beaker twice with ~75 mL of tert-butyl methyl ether, pouring the rinse solution through the funnel each time.
Transfer the product to a 500 mL round-bottom flask and evaporate solvent using a rotary evaporator at room temperature 200 RPM.

Weigh out 37 mg of 2,2'-azobis(2-methylpropionate) (AIBMe), 3.10 g of diethylene glycol methacrylate M(EO)2MA, 0.1 g of oligo ethyleneglycol methacrylate (OEGMA475), 1.30 g of N-(2,2-dimethoxyethyl) acrylamide (DMEMA) and 7.5 µL of thiolglycolic acid (TGA).
Dissolve all reagents in dioxane at a ratio of 5 mL/g total monomer.
Purge the reaction with nitrogen flow for 30 min.
Place flask in a pre-heated oil bath maintained at 75 °C under nitrogen and magnetic stirring at 400 rpm for 4 h.
Remove solvent using a rotary evaporator set to 50 °C and 200 rpm.
Dissolve the polymer product in 100 mL of deionized H2O.
Add 50 mL of 1 M HCl to the dissolved solution.
Stir under magnetic stirring at 400 RPM for 24 hours.
Transfer the polymer solution into dialysis tubing.
Lyophilize the dialyzed sample to obtain a final dried polymer product.
Dissolve hydrazide and aldehyde functionalized polymers separately in 10 mM phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Load each precursor solution (~1 mL each) into separate barrels of a double barrel syringe attached to a static mixer.
Prepare molds of desired thickness, shape, and diameter by punching holes into a silicone rubber sheet.
Mount the silicone mold on a standard glass microscope slide such that holes punched in the mold are completely backed by glass.
Co-extrude the double barrel syringe contents through the static mixer to fill (or slightly overfill) the silicone mold.
Place another standard glass microscope slide on top of the mold and wait for gelation to complete.
Remove the top microscope slide and use a spatula to push the hydrogel away from the silicone rubber mold.
Lift the mold from the lower microscope slide to recover the hydrogels for further testing.
Dehydrate a silicon wafer by heating on a hotplate at 200 °C for 5 min.
Center the wafer on a spin coater.
Apply ~7 mL of SU-8 resist to the wafer.
Ramp the spin speed up to 3000 rpm at a rate of 500 rpm/s.
Hold the speed at 3000 rpm for 30 seconds.
Pre-bake the coating at 65 °C for 10 min.
Soft-bake the coating at 95 °C for 30 min.
Print a photomask on a transparency with the microfluidic pattern defined by Figure 2A.
Insert the photoresist-coated silicon wafer and the photomask in a mask aligner.
Expose the wafer to 365 nm light for 95 s (6.5 W exposure power).
Bake the patterned wafer for 10 min at 95 °C, first by placing it on a hotplate at 65 °C and subsequently heating the hotplate to 95 °C at 10 °C/min.
Place the wafer in a 500 mL beaker containing 100 mL SU-8 developer for at least 10 min, swirling the wafer slowly throughout.
Rinse the patterned wafer with isopropanol.
Dry the patterned wafer with air.
Store the patterned wafer in a cool, dry environment away from light when not in use for soft lithography replica molding.
Place the patterned microfluidic mold in a Petri dish.
Position ~10 mm lengths of L/S 13 silicone tubing on the inlets and outlets of the chip.

Pour ~10 mL of poly(dimethyl siloxane) (PDMS; prepared by mixing Silicone Elastomer Base and Silicone Elastomer Curing Agent in a 10:1 ratio) on top of the chip, carefully avoiding incorporating any PDMS within the placed silicone tubing.
Place the Petri dish in a vacuum chamber for ~10 min to remove air bubbles persisting in and around the patterned structure during curing.
Cure the PDMS by placing the Petri dish containing the patterned mold and uncured PDMS on a hotplate at 85 °C for 2-3 h.
Carefully peel off the cured PDMS from the patterned silicon wafer to expose the soft lithographic patterned PDMS replica of the microfluidic mold.
Place the patterned PDMS and a glass slide upside-down in a high-power plasma cleaner with an air feed.
Apply the plasma at 200 mTorr and 45 W for 90 s to bond the PDMS to the glass slide and create the final microfluidic chip.
Dissolve NIPAM, DMEMA, TGA, and AIBME in ethanol.
Follow steps 2.2.4-2.2.10 for synthesis, changing the reaction temperature to 56 °C in step 2.2.5.
Dissolve PNIPAM-Hzd and PNIPAM-Ald at 6 wt% in deionized water.
Load PNIPAM solutions into separate standard 5 mL syringes.
Dissolve nonionic surfactant (e.g., Span 80) in heavy paraffin oil to a concentration of 1 wt%.
Load the surfactant solution into a standard 60 mL syringe.
Connect PNIPAM solution syringes individually to polymer inlet channels on the microfluidic chip via silicone tubing (~30 cm length per inlet, ~45 cm length per outlet).
Connect paraffin oil solution syringe to the oil inlet channel on the microfluidic chip via silicone tubing.
Deliver oil into the chip at a flow rate between 1.1 mL/h and 5.5 mL/h for priming (typically maintained over a 30 min period) without starting polymer flow.
Use separate infusion syringe pumps to deliver aqueous polymer solutions to the chip at a flow rate of 0.03 mL/h.
Allow the flow system to equilibrate for 30 min to 1 hour to ensure uniform particle formation.
Collect particles in a magnetically stirred round bottom flask until all oil is consumed (12-55 hours).
Stop syringe pumps and clean chip with water if immediate reuse is necessary, but use new chips for separate experiments instead.
Turn off magnetic stirring and allow gel microparticles to settle.
Decant paraffin oil using a pipette.
Wash gel microparticles with pentane (10 mL per 0.5 mL of microparticle volume), mix vigorously for 1 minute, let settle for 1-2 hours, decant residual organic phase.
Repeat washing and settling steps at least five times to remove paraffin oil completely.
Resuspend the gel microparticles in 10 mL deionized water inside a 20 mL glass scintillation vial.
Purge vial with nitrogen overnight to remove residual pentane.
Heat a 5 mL aliquot of the PNIPAM-Hzd stock solution to 70°C using an oil bath under magnetic stirring (350 RPM) inside a 20 mL glass scintillation vial.
Add a 0.25 mL aliquot of PNIPAM-Ald drop-wise into the heated PNIPAM-Hzd solution over a period of 5-10 s.
Continue mixing the solution in the scintillation vials for an additional 15 minutes.
Remove the sample from the oil bath and allow the product to cool to room temperature overnight.
Dialyze the resulting nanogels over 6x6 hour cycles against deionized water using a 3500 kDa MWCO dialysis membrane.
If desired, lyophilize for storage.
Dissolve 50 mg dimethyl 2,2'-azobis(2-methylpropionate) (AIBMe), 4.0 g oligoethyleneglycol methacrylate (OEGMA475), and 0.60 g N-(2,2-dimethoxyethyl) methacrylate (DMEMA) in 20 mL dioxane.
Dissolve POEGMA-Hzd (15 wt%) in deionized water solution.
Dissolve POEGMA-Ald (15 wt%) in deionized water solution.
Dissolve poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO, Mw=600x103 g/mol, 5 wt%) in deionized water.
Mix 1 ml of the PEO solution with each reactive POEGMA solution to create final precursor solutions of 7.5 wt% POEGMA precursor polymer and 2.5 wt% PEO.
Load the two solutions into separate barrels of a double-barrel syringe.
Attach a static mixer and a blunt-tip 18G needle to the double-barrel syringe.
Connect a high-voltage power supply to the blunt-tip needle, grounded at the collector.
Start the syringe pump at a rate of 0.48 ml/h.
Switch on a high voltage of 8.5 kV to perform electrospinning and create nanofibers.
Continue electrospinning as desired to make scaffolds of different thicknesses or until the inlet solutions are exhausted.
Soak the collected scaffolds for 24 hours in deionized water to remove the PEO electrospinning aid.
